about.intro:
Bield is the UK’s one-stop men’s shop and community: kit, knowledge and good company for men who want to get out there and lead. A bield is a Cumbrian word for shelter — the drystone wall or hollow on a fellside where you get out of the weather. It names exactly what we are: somewhere to stop, take stock and set off better equipped.

> Kit is only half of it. The know-how and the good company are what actually get you out the door.

So we lead with knowledge: honest kit tests, route guides and plain-English advice from people who’ve actually used the gear. Gift buyers are a welcome second audience, and everything can be wrapped with a handwritten card — but the man, and getting him out there, comes first.
about.communityLede: Route guides, meet-ups, kit tests and a Journal worth reading — Bield is the people as much as the products.
about.communityText: It’s there in the mark, too: a sheep bield drawn in plan — four short wall arms from a centre, so there’s a lee whatever way the wind comes. Everything points back to getting out there together.

values.title: Warm, not macho
values.body: We talk like a well-travelled friend, never like a kit-list bore.

values.title: Knowledgeable, not technical
values.body: Why it’s good, in one plain sentence. No jargon, no stacked adjectives.

values.title: Wry, not silly
values.body: Dry northern humour, used lightly. No “LAST CHANCE!!!”.

values.title: Honest, not salesy
values.body: Real reviews, clear sizing, no fake countdowns. Ever.

values.title: Made to last
values.body: Quality over quantity. One great jacket beats three average ones.

values.title: Good company
values.body: A community, not a mailing list — get out there, and bring someone.

about.curationTitle: If we wouldn’t use it, it doesn’t go in
about.curationLede: We favour British and independent makers wherever the quality allows, from Borders knitwear to Cumbrian bootmakers.
about.curationText: Every product page answers the same four questions: why it’s good, who it’s for, how it fits, and — for the gift buyer — why it makes a great gift. Plain, useful English throughout.
